scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: A Campus 1 user on VLAN 10 (PC5, 172.16.10.x) reports they
cannot reach hosts on VLAN 30 (172.16.30.x) -- inter-VLAN routing on the Campus 1
multilayer switch seems broken. They suspect one of mswitch0's SVIs
(172.16.10.254 / 172.16.30.254) is down or misconfigured. Please confirm the SVI
fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy; the reported symptom does not exist in the live lab.
All components accused by the ticket were inspected and found correct:

• mswitch0 SVIs: Both vlan10@br0 (172.16.10.254/24) and vlan30@br0
  (172.16.30.254/24) are UP and LOWER_UP. There is no SVI that is
  administratively down or misconfigured.

• L2 path (switch1 → mswitch0 → switch3): switch1 correctly trunks VLAN 10
  (eth0.10, eth1.10 → br_vlan10) to mswitch0. switch3 correctly trunks VLAN 30
  (eth0.30 → br_vlan30) to mswitch0. The switch3 startup script contains an
  editorial comment about a historical translation bug ("eth0.30 was missing")
  but the fix is present in the current running configuration — eth0.30 is UP
  and mswitch0's VLAN 30 SVI MAC is already learned in switch3's forwarding
  database, proving live traffic has traversed the link.

• Routing: mswitch0 holds direct-connected kernel routes for 172.16.10.0/24
  (via vlan10) and 172.16.30.0/24 (via vlan30), and OSPF advertises them
  correctly.

• Firewall: iptables and nftables on mswitch0 are empty (policy ACCEPT).

• End-to-end verification: four independent pings from VLAN 10 hosts (pc5, pc6,
  pc7) to VLAN 30 hosts (pc12, pc13, pc14) all achieved 0% loss with TTL=63,
  confirming correct single-hop inter-VLAN routing through mswitch0.

Root cause: The helpdesk ticket describes a fault that does not exist; the
inter-VLAN routing between VLAN 10 and VLAN 30 is operating normally.

Corrective action: Close the ticket as a false alarm; no configuration change
is required.
